A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cholinergic and GABAergic BF cells are not distributed randomly but in a coextensively distributed manner with the CBP+ cells, and the Parv+ cells are likely the GABAergic cortically projecting cells.

Parv+ neurons are the most likely candidates to be the cortically projecting BF GABAergic neurons; Calb+ neurons are the cortically projecting noncholinergic BF neurons most likely to be GABAergic; and Calret+ neurons are the noncholinergic cortically projecting neurons most likely to contain glutamate.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the basal forebrain (which includes the septum, the vertical and diagonal band of Broca, and the medial septal nucleus) has a much larger population of cortically projecting neurons than previously appreciated.
